Definition: from a derivative probably of G5491; to throw out the lip, i.e. jeer at:--mock.
BiblicalUsage: Chleuazo is to mock, to throw out the lip at someone, and it stands once, in Athens. When Paul speaks of the resurrection of the dead, some mock, while others say they will hear him again, and the gospel divides the crowd on the spot.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the resurrection has always divided hearers, and mockery is the oldest answer to it, yet the gospel is still worth preaching to the mockers in Athens and everywhere else.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
